s1.syndrome_frame: A palpable mass in the outer upper quadrant of the left breast with recent size increase, accompanied by lymph node involvement
salient_findings: Palpable mass in the outer upper quadrant of the left breast
Irregular hypoechoic areas on ultrasound
Patchy tortuous structure with punctate calcification on mammogram
Irregular mass with increased axillary lymph nodes on MRI
Isodense soft tissue mass with abnormal radioactive distribution on PET-CT
key_facts: The patient is a 47-year-old woman
The mass has been present for more than 2 years
The mass has shown obvious size increase over the last half year
No previous medical history
No relevant family history
No history of previous surgery
Ultrasound revealed irregular hypoechoic areas in the left breast
Mammogram showed a patchy tortuous structure in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast
MRI showed an irregular mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast
PET-CT showed an isodense soft tissue mass with abnormal radioactive distribution
Several small lymph nodes in the left axillary region with mildly concentrated radioactivity
No bone, lung, liver, or brain metastasis

shortlist.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common type of breast cancer, consistent with palpable mass and lymph node involvement

shortlist.label: Invasive lobular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Second most common type of breast cancer, also consistent with palpable mass and lymph node involvement

shortlist.label: Phyllodes tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that can present as a palpable mass, with potential for lymph node involvement

shortlist.label: Lymphoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: Less common, but possible cause of palpable mass and lymph node involvement

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive type of breast cancer, consistent with rapid size increase and lymph node involvement

raw.rationale: The combination of imaging findings, including irregular hypoechoic areas on ultrasound, a patchy tortuous structure on mammogram, an irregular mass on MRI, and an isodense soft tissue mass with abnormal radioactive distribution on PET-CT, along with the presence of several small lymph nodes in the left axillary region, are most consistent with invasive ductal carcinoma, which is the most common type of breast cancer and can present with a palpable mass and lymph node involvement.

rejected.label: Invasive lobular carcinoma
rejected.why: Less common than invasive ductal carcinoma and often presents with a more subtle appearance on imaging.

rejected.label: Phyllodes tumor
rejected.why: Typically presents as a large, rapidly growing mass, but imaging characteristics are not as strongly suggestive of malignancy as in this case.

rejected.label: Lymphoma of the breast
rejected.why: Rare and would not typically present with the combination of imaging findings seen in this case.

rejected.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
rejected.why: Characterized by rapid onset of inflammation and swelling of the breast, which is not described in this case.
